title: Function notation
keyIdea: f(x) is the output of the rule f when the input is x.

kid: f(x) = 2x + 3 is a rule. The letter f is its name and x is the input. To find f(4), put 4 in place of x: 2 × 4 + 3 = 11. So f(4) = 11.
f(x) does not mean f times x. Read it as 'f of x': the output when x goes in.
adult: Function notation names a rule and its input. If f(x) = x² − 1, then f(3) = 9 − 1 = 8 and f(−2) = 4 − 1 = 3. The brackets after f show the input. They do not mean multiply.
You can also work backwards. If f(x) = 2x + 3 and f(a) = 11, then 2a + 3 = 11, so a = 4. In context, f(3) = 10 might mean 'after 3 hours, 10 litres are left'.

familyTip: Make a function machine: write a rule like 'double it and add 3', then test each other with inputs.

choices: The output when the input is 5
The input when the output is 5
practice.explain: f(5) is the output of the rule when 5 goes in.

pool.hint: A negative times a negative is positive.

pool.prompt: f(x) = 3x. Sam says f(2) means 'f × 2'. What is wrong?
choices: f(2) means put 2 into the rule, so f(2) = 6

pool.prompt: f(x) = {a}x + {b}. For which x is f(x) = {=a*k+b}?
A taxi ride costs C(m) = 3 + 2m pounds, where m is the number of miles. What does C(5) = 13 mean?
pool.hint: The input is miles; the output is pounds.
pool.explain: C(5) = 13: an input of 5 miles gives an output of £13.

pool.hint: Work out f(3) and f(1) separately.
pool.explain: f(3) = 7 and f(1) = 3, so the sum is 10. It is not f(4) = 9: you can't just add the inputs.
